extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to the American Journal of Health Behavior and media/reporters covering its articles
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and expectations for authors and media about withholding and timing release of study results and related materials for publication in the American Journal of Health Behavior; includes prior-publication (Ingelfinger) restrictions and permitted exceptions for conference presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo is an agreement between author(s) of scientific manuscripts, peer-reviewed journals and reporters concerning the release of information to the media in advance of a specific publication date. The embargo applies to the time between the submission of the manuscript to the publisher and the authorized release of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will defer releasing information and the news media will defer coverage until a specified date set by the publisher (the Am J Health Behav). The embargo exists to ensure journal readers have the full article when the media report on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of parties under embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must defer releasing information and the news media must defer coverage until the specified date set by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mutual deferral is the core requirement of the embargo agreement; deviations undermine the purpose of providing readers the full article at the time of media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for embargo violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters who violate embargo will be excluded from future embargoed information. Authors who violate this embargo will be banned from future publication in the Am J Health Behav.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations trigger sanctions: media exclusion from future embargoes and author publication bans; authors and reporters should therefore adhere strictly to embargo terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional media interviews and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may give interviews to representatives of the media who agree to the Am J Health Behav embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoed information is confidential and cannot be made public by the media until the author has received the final corrected PDF and there are no pending fees. Media interviews are permitted only if the reporter accepts these confidentiality and timing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of embargo — accuracy and fair presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo concept is designed to assure that the information conveyed to broader audiences through these practices is accurate and fairly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should follow these practices when making research results public and not issue premature public statements about their work before it has been published by the Am J Health Behav.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingelfinger Rule — prior publication/submission restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Am J Health Behav does not wish to receive manuscripts on work that has already been presented or published in large part elsewhere or contained in a previous publication; therefore, it fully supports the Ingelfinger Rule. Under this rule, the Am J Health Behav considers publication of the scientific manuscript only on the condition that its key substance has not been submitted or reported elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts whose key substance has been previously submitted or reported elsewhere are ineligible for consideration under this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exception for conference/government presentations and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A key exception to the Ingelfinger Rule is presenting material at scientific conferences, congressional hearings or other government proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While data may have been reported at a scientific meeting, authors must refrain from presenting or handing out copies of author tables, figures and/or illustrations. It is acceptable to talk to reporters at these venues, but comments should be limited to what was addressed in the presentation.
